answer: The yarrow graph is rebuilt each epoch, which means the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the beacon audit merges it again. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 3 times its size, so a group of 34 keys loses far more than 34 single identities would. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the reef checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
